study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissecting task-based fMRI activity using normative modelling: an application to the Emotional Face Matching Task

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To demonstrate that normative modelling of fMRI task-activation can be used to illustrate the influence of different task choices and map replicable individual differences, by building a large-scale reference model of the Emotional Face Matching Task and applying it to a heterogeneous clinical cohort to map individual deviations and relate them to transdiagnostic symptom domains.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Harmonised FSL-based pipeline: gradient unwarping; motion correction; fieldmap-based EPI distortion correction; boundary-based registration of EPI to T1w; ICA-AROMA denoising for motion artifacts; non-linear registration to MNI152 space; resampled to 2mm3 resolution; 5mm FWHM Gaussian kernel spatial smoothing.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The 'fMRI pre-processing' section in the Methods details a harmonized pipeline that was consistently applied across all datasets to minimize variance from processing differences.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Data pre-processing was harmonised across all sites; a FSL-based pipeline 33 was consistently applied... all functional data underwent gradient unwarping, motion correction, fieldmap-based EPI distortion correction (where fieldmaps were available), boundary-based registration of EPI to structural T1-weighted scan, denoising for secondary head motion-related artifacts using automatic noise selection, as implemented in ICA-AROMA 35, non-linear registration into MNI152 space, and grand-mean intensity normalization. Where applicable, datasets were resampled to 2mm3 resolution, and all data were spatially smoothed using a 5 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Exclusion of participants with mean relative RMS > 0.5 mm. For the UK Biobank sample, targeted QC was performed for signal coverage in the prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), selecting the top 5000 participants based on signal presence within specific ROIs.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Participants were excluded if their mean relative RMS was greater than 0.5 mm. Additional quality control was performed for signal coverage in the prefrontal cortex for the UK Biobank sample (see supplementary methods and Supplementary Figs. 2, 3).

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Site effects were handled by including site as a dummy-coded covariate in the Bayesian Linear Regression model. This approach binds the heterogeneous datasets to a common reference model, thereby accounting for site-related variance without requiring explicit data harmonization like ComBat.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: We created normative models of EFMT-related BOLD activation maps, as a function of site, age, sex... We included dummy coded site-related variables as additional covariates of no-interest... A key feature of the normative modelling framework in the context of multi-site fMRI data is that it allows us to aggregate data across multiple samples by binding them to a common reference model. This provides multiple beneﬁts: it removes site effects from the data without requiring the data to be harmonized...

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Voxel-wise Z-score derived from a Normative Probability Map (NPM), representing the difference between true and model-predicted activation, scaled by prediction variance. An extreme deviation was defined by a threshold of |Z| ≥ 2.6.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The Methods section clearly defines the deviation metric, how it's calculated (NPM), and the statistical threshold used to identify significant deviations.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: To estimate a pattern of regional deviations from typical brain function for each participant, we derived a normative probability map (NPM) that quantiﬁes the voxel-wise deviation from the normative model. The subject-speciﬁc Z-score indicates the difference between the predicted activation and true activation scaled by the prediction variance. We thresholded participant's NPM at Z = ± 2.6 (i.e. p < .005)...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Sparse canonical correlation analysis (SCCA) was used to relate whole-brain deviation maps to four transdiagnostic functional domains (negative valence, cognitive function, social processes, arousal/inhibition). A Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare the frequency of extreme deviations between patients and reference controls. For comparison, a traditional voxel-wise case-control GLM was also performed.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of task-fMRI data can map replicable, transdiagnostically-relevant individual differences in brain function that are obscured by traditional group-level analyses.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative models of the Emotional Face Matching Task explained up to 52.5% of variance in BOLD signal in a large reference cohort (N=7728). Individual deviation maps revealed significant inter-individual heterogeneity. In a clinical cohort (N=236), patients showed a higher frequency of extreme deviations for the faces>shapes contrast. Multivariate patterns of deviation were significantly associated with transdiagnostic symptom domains (e.g., negative valence, cognitive function), but not with traditional diagnostic labels. The faces>baseline contrast showed stronger associations with functional domains than the more common faces>shapes contrast, suggesting the choice of contrast is critical for clinical relevance.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The reference sample under-represented individuals in mid-adulthood (ages 37-46). Many predictor variables were collinear across sites, limiting the ability to disentangle specific effects of task parameters. The models are based on cross-sectional data; while test-retest reliability of deviations was moderate-to-good, future work is needed to explicitly model longitudinal change and within-subject variance.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: participants in mid-adulthood (speciﬁcally aged between 37 and 46) were under-represented in our sample... In our sample many predictor variables were collinear across sites which limited our ability to detect systematic differences... While we acknowledge the limitations imposed due to the general limits of test-retest reliability of task fMRI, our results encouragingly show that the deviation scores from a normative model appear replicable over Test-Retest scans.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study demonstrates that normative modeling can be used to disentangle the effects of task design choices (e.g., matching instructions, stimulus sets) on predicted BOLD activation. It also critically highlights that the choice of fMRI contrast (e.g., faces>shapes vs. faces>baseline) is not trivial and that different contrasts can carry complementary information about psychopathology, with faces>baseline showing stronger links to functional domains.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study provides a powerful demonstration of applying normative modeling to large-scale, multi-site task-fMRI data. It successfully binds heterogeneous datasets to a common reference, enabling the analysis of individual differences and their clinical relevance in a transdiagnostic framework that moves beyond traditional case-control statistics. The authors have made their code and group-level statistical maps publicly available, promoting reproducibility.
